from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Classical Search Problem"
        lines = [
            "Searching an unsorted database is a fundamental challenge.",
            "We must check items one by one classically.",
            "Finding one item among N takes O(N) time."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_DEFAULT = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_TARGET = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_COMPLEXITY = "#00FF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_DEFAULT))
        
        # Grid of 10 closed treasure chests labeled 'Search Space'
        search_space_label = Text("Search Space", font_size=24, color=COLOR_DEFAULT)
        self.place_at_grid(search_space_label, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        chests = VGroup()
        positions = [
            "B1", "B2", "B3", "B4", "B5",
            "C1", "C2", "C3", "C4", "C5"
        ]
        
        for pos in positions:
            chest = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=0.7, height=0.5, color=COLOR_DEFAULT)
            lid_line = Line(start=[-0.35, 0.1, 0], end=[0.35, 0.1, 0], color=COLOR_DEFAULT)
            chest_group = VGroup(chest, lid_line)
            self.place_at_grid(chest_group, pos, scale_factor=1.0)
            chests.add(chest_group)

        self.play(Write(search_space_label), FadeIn(chests))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT))
        
        # Highlight chests one by one to show Alice checking them sequentially
        # We will highlight the first 6 chests sequentially
        for i in range(6):
            self.play(
                chests[i].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT),
                run_time=0.4
            )
            self.play(
                chests[i].animate.set_color(COLOR_DEFAULT),
                run_time=0.2
            )
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_COMPLEXITY))
        
        # Change the 7th chest to #FFD700 (Gold)
        target_chest = chests[6]
        self.play(
            target_chest.animate.set_color(COLOR_TARGET),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        
        # Display 'O(N) Complexity'
        complexity_label = Text("O(N) Complexity", font_size=28, color=COLOR_COMPLEXITY)
        self.place_in_area(complexity_label, "E2", "F4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(complexity_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Quantum Superposition", [
            "Quantum computers use superposition to represent all states.",
            "Applying Hadamard gates creates an equal probability distribution.",
            "Every possible answer now exists in parallel."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show 10 vertical bars of equal height in #00BFFF with 'Probability Amplitude' label.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))
        
        bars = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(height=2.0, width=0.3, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color="#00BFFF", color="#00BFFF") 
            for _ in range(10)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_in_area(bars, "B1", "E6")
        
        label = Text("Probability Amplitude", font_size=24, color="#00BFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(label, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        label.shift(RIGHT * 0.5) # Center label better across A1-A6 area
        
        self.play(Create(bars), Write(label), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Pulse all bars simultaneously in #FFFFFF to represent a Hadamard transform.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF")
        )
        
        self.play(
            AnimationGroup(*[Indicate(bar, color="#FFFFFF", scale_factor=1.1) for bar in bars]),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Maintain the uniform heights to show the system is in a state of 'all chests partially open'.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00BFFF")
        )
        
        # Visualizing "all chests partially open" by adding a slight glow or simple highlight
        glow_bars = bars.copy().set_color("#FFFFFF").set_opacity(0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(glow_bars), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeOut(glow_bars), run_time=1)
        
        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define the title and lecture lines for Section 3
        title_text = "Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "We use an Oracle to identify the correct answer.",
            "The Oracle recognizes the target state without measuring.",
            "It flips the sign of the target's probability amplitude.",
            "This process is known as phase inversion.",
            "Other states remain completely unchanged by the Oracle."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        TARGET_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        FLIPPED_COLOR = "#FF4500"
        NORMAL_COLOR = WHITE
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a collection of white vertical bars representing quantum states.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(NORMAL_COLOR)
        bars = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(width=0.4, height=1.0, color=NORMAL_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=2) 
            for _ in range(8)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(bars, 'C1', 'C6')
        
        self.play(Create(bars), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight one specific bar (the 4th) with the label 'Target' in #FFD700.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(TARGET_COLOR)
        target_bar = bars[3]
        target_label = Text("Target", font_size=20, color=TARGET_COLOR)
        # Position label above the target bar near grid B4
        self.place_at_grid(target_label, 'B4')
        
        self.play(
            target_bar.animate.set_color(TARGET_COLOR),
            Write(target_label),
            run_time=1.0
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Slowly flip the target bar across the X-axis so it points downwards.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(FLIPPED_COLOR)
        
        # Calculate the base y-coordinate (X-axis) at the boundary between Row C and Row D.
        # Row C center is 0.2, Row D center is -0.8. Boundary is at -0.3.
        # Since bars are height 1.0 and centered at 0.2, their bottom is exactly at -0.3.
        base_y = -0.3
        flip_point = np.array([target_bar.get_center()[0], base_y, 0])
        
        self.play(
            target_bar.animate.scale(np.array([1, -1, 1]), about_point=flip_point).set_color(FLIPPED_COLOR),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Change the color of the flipped bar to #FF4500 and show a dashed line at Y=0.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(FLIPPED_COLOR)
        
        # Create a dashed line representing the zero-amplitude axis.
        # We place it in the area bridging row C and D to center it at y=-0.3.
        dashed_line = DashedLine(
            start=self.grid['C1'] + LEFT * 0.5,
            end=self.grid['C6'] + RIGHT * 0.5,
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=2
        )
        line_container = VGroup(dashed_line)
        self.place_in_area(line_container, 'C1', 'D6')
        
        # The flip happened in line 3, so here we focus on the dashed line and title/label emphasis.
        self.play(Create(dashed_line), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Pulse the other white bars to show they are unaffected.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        
        others = VGroup(*[bars[i] for i in range(len(bars)) if i != 3])
        self.play(
            others.animate.set_color(WHITE).scale(1.1),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Step 2: The Diffusion Operator (Inversion about the Mean)",
            [
                "Next, we apply the Grover diffusion operator.",
                "It performs an inversion about the average amplitude.",
                "The target's negative amplitude is pushed far above average.",
                "Meanwhile, all incorrect amplitudes are significantly reduced.",
                "This amplification makes the target state much more likely."
            ]
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the bars from the previous step (one down, others up).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Define bars
        bar_w = 0.6
        bar1 = Rectangle(width=bar_w, height=1.0, fill_opacity=0.8, color="#888888", fill_color="#888888")
        bar2 = Rectangle(width=bar_w, height=1.0, fill_opacity=0.8, color="#888888", fill_color="#888888")
        bar3 = Rectangle(width=bar_w, height=1.0, fill_opacity=0.8, color="#888888", fill_color="#888888")
        bar4 = Rectangle(width=bar_w, height=1.0, fill_opacity=0.8, color="#FFFF00", fill_color="#FFFF00")
        
        self.place_in_area(bar1, 'C2', 'D2')
        self.place_in_area(bar2, 'C3', 'D3')
        self.place_in_area(bar3, 'C4', 'D4')
        self.place_in_area(bar4, 'D5', 'E5')
        
        bars = VGroup(bar1, bar2, bar3, bar4)
        self.play(Create(bars))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw a horizontal dashed line in #7CFC00 representing the 'Mean' amplitude.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#7CFC00")
        
        mean_y_start = (self.grid["C1"] + self.grid["D1"]) / 2
        mean_y_end = (self.grid["C6"] + self.grid["D6"]) / 2
        mean_line = DashedLine(start=mean_y_start, end=mean_y_end, color="#7CFC00")
        
        mean_label = Text("Mean", font_size=18, color="#7CFC00")
        self.place_at_grid(mean_label, "C6")
        
        self.play(Create(mean_line), Write(mean_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The target's negative amplitude is pushed far above average.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Target's distance indicator
        arrow_start = (self.grid["C5"] + self.grid["D5"]) / 2
        arrow_end = self.grid["E5"]
        dist_arrow = DoubleArrow(
            start=arrow_start,
            end=arrow_end,
            buff=0,
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=2
        )
        
        self.play(Create(dist_arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Flip all bars across the mean line; the target bar becomes very tall.
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#888888")
        
        new_bar1 = Rectangle(width=bar_w, height=0.01, fill_opacity=0.8, color="#888888", fill_color="#888888")
        new_bar2 = Rectangle(width=bar_w, height=0.01, fill_opacity=0.8, color="#888888", fill_color="#888888")
        new_bar3 = Rectangle(width=bar_w, height=0.01, fill_opacity=0.8, color="#888888", fill_color="#888888")
        new_bar4 = Rectangle(width=bar_w, height=2.0, fill_opacity=0.8, color="#FFFF00", fill_color="#FFFF00")
        
        self.place_at_grid(new_bar1, 'D2')
        self.place_at_grid(new_bar2, 'D3')
        self.place_at_grid(new_bar3, 'D4')
        self.place_in_area(new_bar4, 'B5', 'D5')
        
        self.play(
            Transform(bar1, new_bar1),
            Transform(bar2, new_bar2),
            Transform(bar3, new_bar3),
            Transform(bar4, new_bar4),
            FadeOut(dist_arrow),
            FadeOut(mean_line),
            FadeOut(mean_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(bar4.animate.set_color("#00FF00").set_fill("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Indicate(bar4, color="#00FF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        # Changed Tex to Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        title = Text("Grover's Algorithm: Time Complexity", font_size=36, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Lecture Content
        # Removed LaTeX math delimiters ($) for Text compatibility
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Comparison of Search Efficiency",
            "- Classical Search: O(N) operations",
            "- Grover's Search: O(sqrt(N)) operations",
            "- Quadratic speedup for unstructured databases"
        ]
        
        lecture_vgroup = VGroup(*[
            Text(line, font_size=28, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines
        ]).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        
        lecture_vgroup.to_edge(LEFT, buff=1.0).shift(DOWN * 0.5)

        # 3. Visual Representation (Grid/Bar Chart)
        # Showing the difference between N and sqrt(N) for N=16
        n_val = 16
        sqrt_n_val = 4

        classical_box = Rectangle(height=0.5, width=n_val * 0.2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        # Changed Tex to Text
        classical_label = Text("Classical: N=16", font_size=24).next_to(classical_box, UP)
        classical_group = VGroup(classical_box, classical_label)

        quantum_box = Rectangle(height=0.5, width=sqrt_n_val * 0.2, color=GOLD, fill_opacity=0.5)
        # Changed Tex to Text
        quantum_label = Text("Quantum: sqrt(N)=4", font_size=24).next_to(quantum_box, UP)
        quantum_group = VGroup(quantum_box, quantum_label)

        visual_content = VGroup(classical_group, quantum_group).arrange(DOWN, buff=1.2)
        visual_content.to_edge(RIGHT, buff=1.5).shift(DOWN * 0.5)

        # 4. Animations
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(0.5)

        for line in lecture_vgroup:
            self.play(FadeIn(line, shift=RIGHT * 0.2), run_time=0.8)
        
        self.wait(1)

        self.play(
            Create(classical_box),
            Write(classical_label)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(
            Create(quantum_box),
            Write(quantum_label)
        )
        
        # Highlight difference
        arrow = DoubleArrow(
            classical_box.get_right(), 
            quantum_box.get_right(), 
            color=RED, 
            stroke_width=2
        )
        # Changed Tex to Text
        speedup_text = Text("Quadratic Speedup", font_size=22, color=RED).next_to(arrow, RIGHT)
        
        self.play(Create(arrow), Write(speedup_text))
        self.wait(3)

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Quantum Speedup & Conclusion"
        lines = [
            "We only need roughly square root of N iterations.",
            "This provides a massive quadratic speedup over classical methods.",
            "Measuring the system now reveals the correct answer."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a comparison table of 'Classical: 1,000,000' vs 'Quantum: 1,000' in #FFFFFF.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        classical_text = Text("Classical: 1,000,000", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        quantum_text = Text("Quantum: 1,000", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        comparison = VGroup(classical_text, quantum_text).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(comparison, "A1", "B6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(comparison))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display a green progress bar filling to '31 steps' to represent O(sqrt(N)) speedup.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        bar_width = 3.5
        bar_bg = Rectangle(width=bar_width, height=0.4, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        bar_fill = Rectangle(width=0.01, height=0.4, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0)
        bar_fill.align_to(bar_bg, LEFT)
        
        bar_group = VGroup(bar_bg, bar_fill)
        self.place_in_area(bar_group, "C1", "D6")
        
        bar_label = Text("31 steps", font_size=22, color=GREEN)
        bar_label.next_to(bar_group, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        sqrt_n_label = Text("O(√N)", font_size=28, color=GREEN)
        sqrt_n_label.next_to(bar_group, UP, buff=0.3)
        
        self.play(
            Create(bar_bg),
            Write(sqrt_n_label)
        )
        self.play(
            bar_fill.animate.stretch_to_fit_width(bar_width, about_edge=LEFT),
            FadeIn(bar_label),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade in a solid Golden Key icon in #FFD700 to represent the final measurement.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # Golden Key representation using basic shapes
        key_handle = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#FFD700", stroke_width=4)
        key_shaft = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=0.1, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0)
        key_shaft.next_to(key_handle, RIGHT, buff=0)
        notch1 = Rectangle(width=0.08, height=0.15, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0)
        notch1.move_to(key_shaft.get_right() + LEFT*0.1 + DOWN*0.1)
        notch2 = Rectangle(width=0.08, height=0.15, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0)
        notch2.move_to(key_shaft.get_right() + LEFT*0.25 + DOWN*0.1)
        
        golden_key = VGroup(key_handle, key_shaft, notch1, notch2)
        self.place_in_area(golden_key, "E2", "F5", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(golden_key, scale=1.5))
        self.play(Flash(golden_key, color="#FFD700", line_length=0.3, num_lines=12))
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Grover's Algorithm: Finding a Needle in a Quantum Haystack
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic understanding of linear algebra and quantum states.

sections.title: The Classical Search Problem
sections.content: Introduce the concept of an unstructured search. In a database of N items, finding a specific entry classically takes N/2 attempts on average and N attempts in the worst case (O(N)).
sections.example: Imagine a character named 'Alice' looking for a specific Golden Key hidden inside one of 1,000 identical-looking treasure chests. Classically, she must open them one by one.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Quantum Superposition
sections.content: Explain that a quantum computer doesn't check boxes one by one. Using a Hadamard transform, we put the system into a uniform superposition where every chest is 'partially open' simultaneously. Visualize this as a set of equal-length vertical bars on a graph, representing the probability amplitude of each chest.
sections.example: Instead of opening one chest, Alice uses a 'Quantum Lens' to see a blurry ghost of all 1,000 chests at once, all having the same height (probability).

sections.title: Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)
sections.content: Introduce the 'Oracle' function. It recognizes the target and flips its sign (mathematically, a reflection across the plane perpendicular to the target state). Graphically, the bar representing the 'Golden Key' flips from pointing up to pointing down, while others stay the same.
sections.example: The Oracle is like a 'Magic Magnet' that doesn't pull the Golden Key out, but simply paints its ghost-image a different color (negative phase) without changing its size.

sections.title: Step 2: The Diffusion Operator (Inversion about the Mean)
sections.content: Explain the Grover Diffusion Operator. It flips all amplitudes around the average value of all amplitudes. Since the target is now negative, the average is slightly lowered. Flipping around this mean causes the target's amplitude to grow significantly while others shrink.
sections.example: Visualize a horizontal line representing the 'Average Height'. When we flip every bar across this line, the 'flipped' Golden Key bar shoots way above the rest, while the wrong chests shrink toward the floor.

sections.title: The Geometric View: Vector Rotation
sections.content: Translate the bar flips into a 2D geometric rotation. Represent the state as a vector moving from the 'All Possibilities' axis toward the 'Target' axis. Each Grover iteration (Oracle + Diffusion) rotates the vector by a specific angle θ toward the solution.
sections.example: Think of a clock hand. The Oracle and Diffusion acts as a 'tick', pushing the hand closer to the 12 o'clock position (the Golden Key) with every step.

sections.title: Quantum Speedup & Conclusion
sections.content: Explain that we only need approximately π/4 * √N iterations to reach the solution. This is a quadratic speedup: O(√N). For 1,000,000 items, a classical computer takes 1,000,000 checks, but Grover's takes only about 1,000.
sections.example: Alice finds her Golden Key in 31 steps instead of 1,000. She measures the system, and the 'ghost' of the Golden Key collapses into the real, solid key with nearly 100% certainty.

storyboard.title: The Classical Search Problem
lecture_lines: Searching an unsorted database is a fundamental challenge.
We must check items one by one classically.
Finding one item among N takes O(N) time.
animations: Display a grid of 10 closed treasure chests labeled 'Search Space' in #FFFFFF.
Highlight chests one by one in #FFFF00 to show Alice checking them sequentially.
Change the 7th chest to #FFD700 and display 'O(N) Complexity' in #00FF00.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Quantum Superposition
lecture_lines: Quantum computers use superposition to represent all states.
Applying Hadamard gates creates an equal probability distribution.
Every possible answer now exists in parallel.
animations: Show 10 vertical bars of equal height in #00BFFF with 'Probability Amplitude' label.
Pulse all bars simultaneously in #FFFFFF to represent a Hadamard transform.
Maintain the uniform heights to show the system is in a state of 'all chests partially open'.

storyboard.title: Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)
lecture_lines: We use an Oracle to identify the correct answer.
The Oracle recognizes the target state without measuring.
It flips the sign of the target's probability amplitude.
This process is known as phase inversion.
Other states remain completely unchanged by the Oracle.
animations: Show a collection of white vertical bars representing quantum states.
Highlight one specific bar (the 4th) with the label 'Target' in #FFD700.
Slowly flip the target bar across the X-axis so it points downwards.
Change the color of the flipped bar to #FF4500 and show a dashed line at Y=0.
Pulse the other white bars to show they are unaffected.

storyboard.title: Step 2: The Diffusion Operator (Inversion about the Mean)
lecture_lines: Next, we apply the Grover diffusion operator.
It performs an inversion about the average amplitude.
The target's negative amplitude is pushed far above average.
Meanwhile, all incorrect amplitudes are significantly reduced.
This amplification makes the target state much more likely.
animations: Display the bars from the previous step (one down, others up).
Draw a horizontal dashed line in #7CFC00 representing the 'Mean' amplitude.
Show the target bar's distance from the mean line to prepare for the flip.
Flip all bars across the mean line; the target bar becomes very tall.
Highlight the tall target bar in #00FF00 to show its dominance.

storyboard.title: The Geometric View: Vector Rotation
lecture_lines: We can visualize Grover's algorithm as a geometric rotation.
The quantum state starts far from the target vector.
Each iteration rotates the state toward the solution.
The Oracle and Diffusion together create this rotation.
The state vector gradually aligns with the target state.
animations: Display a 2D plane with white axes labeled $|s\rangle$ and $|w\rangle$.
Draw the initial state vector $|\psi\rangle$ in #FF00FF close to the $|s\rangle$ axis.
Show the vector rotating by an angle $\theta$ toward the $|w\rangle$ axis.
Overlay a text box 'Oracle + Diffusion' to show the cause of rotation.
Show the vector landing almost perfectly on the $|w\rangle$ axis.

storyboard.title: Quantum Speedup & Conclusion
lecture_lines: We only need roughly square root of N iterations.
This provides a massive quadratic speedup over classical methods.
Measuring the system now reveals the correct answer.
animations: Show a comparison table of 'Classical: 1,000,000' vs 'Quantum: 1,000' in #FFFFFF.
Display a green progress bar filling to '31 steps' to represent $O(\sqrt{N})$ speedup.
Fade in a solid Golden Key icon in #FFD700 to represent the final measurement.
